_note: Digging on the street map (ui/innerMapDigging.js): holes, filling them in, graves. Seconds are real seconds of work at the spot; carrying a set of tools (any item id in 'tools') multiplies them by toolSpeed. 'finds' are rolled once per hole, in order: the first whose chance hits is found.

finds.text: Your spade turns up {gold} gold coins, buried long ago.
You turn up a broken clay pot. Nothing of worth.
An old bone, brown with age. Best not to wonder whose.

text.dig: You dig a hole, the spoil heaped beside it.
text.fill: You shovel the earth back in and tread it down.
text.bury: You lay {name} in the hole and heap the earth over them.
text.exhume: You dig {name} back up out of the grave.
respects: You stand a while by {name}'s grave.
You bow your head over {name}'s grave.
You say a word for {name}, {years} in the ground.
respectsMound: You stand a while by the bare mound where {name} lies.
You bow your head over the turned earth. Only you know it is {name} under it.

_burial: A body buried by the player (world/burials.js; ui/innerMapDigging.js) is a plain, unmarked mound: named 'Burial Mound', not the grave of anyone. freshDays: days a mound is bare, dark, freshly turned earth (no grass, no flowers) before it weathers into the churchyard's grassed mound; settleDays: days for an unmarked mound to settle level and the ground to grow back over it (drawn fading down to minAlpha; the record stays: still dug up, still marked). markers: what may be raised over it, the churchyards' kinds (data/graves.json markers, their art): item, a marker carried in the pack (bought at a market: grave carvers and masons make them, data/markets.json), used up when raised; carve, the wood or planks carried that a cross is carved from on the spot (the first the player has); seconds / carveSeconds the work at the spot. Dug up, a marker comes back to the pack as its item. Burials are saved on world.burials[hex]['q,r'].

text.marked: You raise a {marker} over {name}. It is a grave now, with a name on it.
text.carved: You carve a rough {marker}, cut {name}'s name into it and set it at the head of the mound.
text.alreadyMarked: A marker already stands over this grave.
